newsitem.title: GERMANY: Horta says Bonn lets trade obstruct Timor stance.
newsitem.headline: Horta says Bonn lets trade obstruct Timor stance.

text.p: Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos Horta accused Germany on Wednesday of letting trade links with Indonesia dictate an attitude of indifference to the self-determination for East Timor which he is campaigning for.
"So far the position of the German government is very low-key, very distant, almost to the point of indifference," he told Reuters after a meeting with German parliamentary speaker Rita Suessmuth.
"German has very strong trade and economic links with Indonesia and that seems to dictate its position on East Timor as well," said Ramos Horta, who lives in self-imposed exile in Australia.
"Germany could play a much more active and constructive role in forcing the Indonesian government to respect human rights in East Timor."
The Foreign Ministry said a crisis surrounding a diplomatic hostage-taking in Peru had prevented Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel meeting Ramos Horta.

East Timor, with a mainly Catholic population of more than 800,000 people, was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed a year later. The United Nations did not recognise the takeover and regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.
On Monday Chancellor Helmut Kohl met East Timor's Catholic bishop Carlos Belo, who shared this year's Nobel Prize with Ramos Horta in recognition of their peaceful struggle for self-determination.

Belo made no comment on Germany's stance. Kohl, who visited Indonesia earlier this year, spoke of the importance of a peaceful and just settlement for East Timor involving respect for its human rights and cultural identity.
